subject.title: fix(agents): prevent opaque shell commands bypassing auto-review

question: Should OpenClaw accept the intentional compatibility change that routes PowerShell profile/login/encoded and opaque shell-carrier commands from model auto-review to required human approval after latest-head proof is attached?
rationale: The patch tightens a security boundary but can change established automatic-execution behavior; maintainer intent is needed to accept that tradeoff and the protected review state.

options.title: Land after refreshed proof
options.body: Rebase onto current main and provide redacted latest-head host approval evidence for blocked and preserved command classes before accepting the tighter human-approval boundary.

options.title: Narrow the blocked classes
options.body: Keep only carriers whose startup or payload behavior is demonstrably opaque if maintainers do not want to change auto-review eligibility for all profile or login invocations.

options.title: Pause for boundary design
options.body: Hold the PR if the desired long-term contract between automatic review and startup-capable shells remains unsettled.

recommendation.title: Land after refreshed proof
recommendation.body: Rebase onto current main and provide redacted latest-head host approval evidence for blocked and preserved command classes before accepting the tighter human-approval boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged baseline and this follow-up establish the strongest available feature-history connection to the affected review boundary.
